claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure containing dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy exhibits brittle behavior and limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcracking, and premature catastrophic failure in the untreated alloy.
A single-step intermediate-temperature anneal under an inert atmosphere is the proposed intervention.
Annealing below the full-recrystallization temperature can activate recovery while limiting excessive phase coarsening and deleterious reactions.
Intermediate-temperature annealing will relax or modify internal boundary structures and reduce their tendency to accumulate dislocations.
The anneal may form fine precipitates that hinder crack initiation.
The annealing treatment will relieve residual stresses near lamellar interfaces.
The annealing treatment will enable recovery and limited recrystallization near lamellar interfaces.
Recovery and limited interfacial recrystallization will reduce local yield-strength variations and dislocation accumulation.
Reduced dislocation accumulation will lower stress concentrations and suppress microcracking during tensile loading.
The treated alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile elongation than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will maintain or modestly increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Excessive recrystallization or coarse precipitate formation could compromise strength or other performance metrics, particularly at elevated temperatures.
